    AI Overview
    March 31 is primarily recognized as Cesar Chavez Day (or Farmworkers Day) in the U.S., honoring the birth and legacy of the labor leader. It is also widely celebrated as the International Transgender Day of Visibility, along with several fun observances like National Crayon Day, World Backup Day, and National Tater Day. 
    Key March 31 Observances: 
    • Cesar Chavez Day/Farmworkers Day: Celebrates the birthday of the American labor leader and civil rights activist.
    • International Transgender Day of Visibility: Dedicated to celebrating transgender people and raising awareness of discrimination.
    • World Backup Day: Encourages people to back up their data to prevent loss.
    • National Crayon Day: A fun day celebrating the invention of crayons.
    • National Tater Day: A day to celebrate tater tots and potatoes.
    • National Prom Day: A day to celebrate and remember high school proms. 
    Note: In 2026, some locations in California have renamed Cesar Chavez Day to "Farmworkers Day" or "Farm Workers Appreciation Day".

    What's celebrated on March 31st?

    AI Overview
    View all
    March 31 is primarily observed as the International Transgender Day of Visibility (TDoV), a day dedicated to celebrating the lives, contributions, and resilience of transgender people while raising awareness of discrimination. It is also widely recognized as World Backup Day, encouraging digital data safety. 
    Key Celebrations and Observances for March 31:
     
    • International Transgender Day of Visibility: Focuses on celebrating trans rights, leadership, and visibility globally.
    • World Backup Day: A reminder to back up documents, photos, and digital files to prevent data loss.
    • Cesar Chavez Day: Observed in the US to honor the labor leader's legacy and advocacy for farmworkers.
    • National Days (USA):
      • National Crayon Day: Celebrating creativity.
      • National Tater Day: A day honoring potatoes.
      • National Prom Day: Celebrating memories and friendship.
      • National Clams on the Half Shell Day: A food appreciation day.
      • National Bunsen Burner Day: Celebrating the birthday of Robert Bunsen.
    • Cultural & Religious: Occasionally falls on or near festivals like Holi (sometimes celebrated as Rang-Holi) and sometimes marks Easter depending on the year. 
    These days encourage awareness, digital preparedness, and celebration of diverse cultural and personal milestones.
